Have you seen them all? I have not seen them all; my eyes grew tired. Fall asleep now; the stars are watching you.

english: Mother-in-law, when will my husband return home? He said: “When the moon is full, I shall return home.” Tonight the moon is half full. Wait seven nights. Then he will arrive. I fear the wolves on the road. Do not be afraid, daughter-in-law; your husband is strong. The gods guard him.

english: Father, tell me: where does the sun go in the evening? It sinks under the earth. In the night it walks back toward the dawn. Who carries the sun? The old men say this. Swift horses draw the wheel of the sun. Have you seen those horses? I have not seen them. But in the morning I see the light.

english: Of-Good-Fame, I do not see the moon tonight. Clouds cover it. Soon it will rain. Then let us drive the sheep to the village. Let us drive them. Where is your dog? He is lying by the fire. A sluggish dog! Lead him here.

english: Uncle, why are you waiting? I am waiting for the full moon. In its light I will hunt the wild beasts. Will you lead me with you? I will lead you, if you keep silent. I will keep silent; I will not speak. Good. Fall asleep now; we are going at night.

pie: kʷóm póh₂imen ḱós péh₂uros wetsós ǵn̥h₁yéto? néwoy méh₁nsi h₁nédʰt tísrn̥s nókʷtn̥s gʷíh₃weti. h₁ésyo méh₂tēr h₁éneh₂ albʰéh₂ gʷṓws. wetsós h₂mélǵos píph₃eti. píph₃eti bʰuHyéti-kʷe. sh₁séni ḱuh₁rós uksḗn h₁éseti. nu stéh₂dʰh₁om wodʰéyēti. ḱóm wetsóm wéḱsi? h₁ím wéḱmi. nu moy h₂ówim h₁ésmi h₂m̥bʰí dh₃dʰí.
english: Herdsman, when was this little calf born? It came forth at the new moon; it has lived three nights. Its mother is that white cow. The calf drinks milk. It drinks, and it grows. At harvest time it will be a strong bull. Then it will lead the herd! Do you want this calf? I want it! Then give me a sheep for it.

pie: ǵérh₂ont ḱód dóru steh₂róm. kʷóti ǵʰéyomn̥s stestóh₂e? h₁íd méd sényos. h₂éwh₂osyo moy ph₂tḗr h₁íd dʰǵʰémi dʰéh₁t. nu polh₁úns h₃réǵn̥s dedórḱe. h₃réǵn̥s kéh₃tuns-kʷe dedórḱe éti-kʷe stestóh₂e. suHnéwes toy ḱósyo dréws sḱh₃yéh₂i sédyoyh₁ent. ḱm̥tóm ǵʰéymn̥h₂ stesth₂yéh₁t.
english: Old man, this tree is stout. How many winters has it stood? It is older than I. My grandfather's father set it in the earth. Then it has seen many kings. It has seen kings and battles, and it is still standing. May your sons sit in the shade of this tree. May it stand for a hundred winters!

pie: tósyo ǵʰéwtorm̥ prēḱst: "súHnus moy ǵn̥h₁yetōd!"
english: He asked his priest: "May a son be born to me!"

english: King, when shall we worship the gods? When the new moon is born. Then the year turns, and the days grow long. What shall I bring? Bring a white sheep and milk. I will bring them both. Will you pour the mead? I will pour it, and we will sing to Sky.

pie: kʷóti ǵʰéyomn̥s h₂éwh₂e dedórḱth₂e? népot pl̥h₁éwih₂n̥s ǵʰéyomn̥s dedórḱh₂e. dl̥h₁gʰéh₂m ǵʰéyōm memónh₂e. snóygʷʰos méǵh₂s h₁ést polh₁éwes-kʷe gʷówes m̥rént. bʰéyh₂s? bʰéyh₂m̥. swésōr moy n̥smé ph₂wéni h₁épi gʷʰr̥néwt. kʷíd népot túH memónth₂e? tísrn̥s ǵʰéyomn̥s memónh₂e. ḱm̥tóm ǵʰéyomn̥s widóyh₁s.
english: Grandfather, how many winters have you seen? I have seen many winters, grandson. I remember a long winter. The snow was great, and many cattle died. Were you afraid? I was afraid. My sister warmed us by the fire. And you, grandson, what do you remember? I remember three winters. May you see a hundred winters!

pie: méh₂ter gólesi ph₂wéni h₁épi l̥gʰdʰí. dʰúgh₂ter ǵr̥h₂éntih₂ h₁ésmi ǵʰéyomes moy pl̥h₁éwih₂es. wósr̥ widḗsi. h₂éndʰesh₂ h₁nédʰeti? h₁nédʰeti sh₂wéni-kʷe sédyēsi. kúdʰe toy bʰréh₂tēr h₁ésti? h₂éǵroy gʷéwbʰis ḱóm h₁ésti. dʰúgh₂ter moy te deywṓs ḱluwih₁ént.
english: Mother, you are cold; lie down by the fire. I am old, daughter; my winters are many. You will see the spring. Will the flowers come forth? They will come forth, and you will sit in the sun. Where is your brother? He is in the field with the cattle. May the gods hear you, my daughter.

pie: nu h₃réḱs pótnih₂ súHnum ǵeǵonh₁e.
english: The king's lady bore a son.

english: Father, wake up! The dawn has come. Has it grown light? It has grown light in the east, and the birds are singing. Then bring me water, and let us yoke the oxen. Where are we going today? To the far field. We will plough it before the heat. Your sister will give us porridge in the field.

english: Father, you are weary. Shall I bring you water? Bring nothing, son. Sit with me. I have lived many summers and winters. Soon I will go to the gods. Do not say that! Remember me, son, when the year turns. I will remember you in the winters.

pie: h₂éwh₂e moy h₂ǵdʰí kʷíd ǵʰéymn̥h₂ góleti? sóh₂wl̥ ǵʰiméni n̥sméd h₂epó stéygʰeti. h₁ésyo stóygʰos mr̥ǵʰús. sémeh₂i? sémeh₂i dʰégʷʰh₂t dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe gʷʰr̥néwti. kʷóterom lubʰyési? sémeh₂m lubʰyóh₂ nu nókʷtes mr̥ǵʰéwih₂es. ǵʰéymn̥ lubʰyóh₂ nu ph₂wéni h₁épi sédyomes spéleh₂-kʷe wérh₁yomes.
english: Grandfather, tell me: why is the winter cold? In winter the sun walks away from us. Its path is short. And in summer? In summer it comes near, and it warms the earth. Which of the two do you love? I love the summer; then the nights are short. I love the winter; then we sit by the fire and tell stories.

english: Sister, a star fell from the sky! Where did it fall? Into the river. Then a great man has died. My grandmother used to say this. Is that true? I do not know. The gods know it. Was the star bright? It was white and swift.

english: It is getting dark, sister-in-law. Do you see that bright star? I see it. It is the star of the evening. When it appears, the herdsmen lead the cattle to the village. Then let us leave the wool and cook the meat. Let us cook; my husband will be hungry. My husband eats the meat of three men!

pie: kʷíd ǵń̥h₃ra gʷḗn mḗh₁n̥s? mḗh₁n̥s lówksneh₂s stóygʰos. lówksneh₂ ǵeǵónh₁e h₂wékst néḱt-kʷe. kʷíd yóh₁r̥? yóh₁r̥ ǵʰéyōm sémeh₂-kʷe. kʷíd prḗḱs? ǵn̥h₃rós bʰuHyéh₁m̥. ǵn̥h₃rós bʰúHesi h₁yód ḱléwsēsi.
english: Wise woman, what is a month? A month is the path of the moon. The moon is born, it grows, and it vanishes. And what is a year? A year is a winter and a summer. Why did you ask? May I become wise! You will become wise, if you listen.

pie: ǵérh₂ont sóh₂wl̥ néḱt. témHos dʰéǵʰōm stégeti. mógʰew mē tréses. ḱód widóm h₁yód h₂yuHn̥ḱós h₁ésm̥. nu sóh₂wl̥ h₂éti gʷémt? h₂éti gʷémt mórtōs-kʷe mudént. dyḗm ph₂térm̥ h₁yáǵōmes. h₁ím h₁yáǵōmes léwkm̥ nos dh₃yéh₁t.
english: Elder, the sun has vanished! Darkness covers the earth! Do not tremble, boy. I saw this when I was young. Did the sun come back then? It came back, and the people rejoiced. Let us worship Sky, the father. Let us worship him; may he give us the light!

english: Master of the house, the darkness is coming. Shall I sit at your hearth? Sit, guest, and be dear to us. Who are you, and where are you going? I am a herdsman; I am going to the king. The king's house is far. Rest here, and early in the morning go on. You are good to me; may the gods give you good things.

pie: príHe yóh₁r̥ wértetor. nókʷtes dl̥h₁gʰéh₂es dinṓs-kʷe mr̥ǵʰéwes. sóh₂wl̥ moḱs h₂éti gʷémeti. nu dh₂pnóm h₂réydʰōmes. kʷíd deywóybʰos déh₃ete? uksénm̥ sweh₂dú-kʷe médʰu. nu nos dyḗws h₁wésu yóh₁r̥ dh₃yéh₁t. dh₂pnóm swéh₂h₁ pótn̥yeh₂h₁ ḱóm gʷm̥dʰí. gʷm̥yṓmes pótnih₂-kʷe moy kh₂nḗti.
english: Friend, the year is turning. The nights are long, and the days are short. Soon the sun will come back. Then we will prepare a feast. What will you give to the gods? A bull and sweet mead. Then may Sky give us a good year! Come to the feast with your wife! We will come, and my wife will sing.

pie: kʷóm me méh₂ter wiHrós dṓm wédʰētes? dʰúgh₂ter h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂ éti h₁ési. tísrn̥s sémās méne. tód dweh₂róm. h₁íd mr̥ǵʰú. pénkʷe sémās ménom. nu moy ph₂tḗr h₁ludʰét? déḱm̥ gʷéwbʰis ḱóm h₁ludʰét dṓm-kʷe me wédʰet.
english: Mother, when will a man lead me home? You are still young, daughter. Wait three summers. That is long! It is short. I waited five summers. And then my father arrived? He arrived with ten cows, and he led me home.

pie: kʷóm méh₂ter ǵn̥h₁yóh₂e? ǵʰyémi h₂ewsér ǵn̥h₁yéth₂e. snóygʷʰos dʰǵʰémi légʰet dyḗws-kʷe h₁rudʰéh₁t. kʷóti ǵʰéyomn̥s gʷíh₃woh₂? swéḱs ǵʰéyomn̥s. h₂ówins moḱs swóh₁ h₂éwh₂oh₁ ḱóm péh₂sesi. h₂éwh₂os moy h₁mé ḱéHseti? ḱéHseti te h₁éwkesi-kʷe.
english: Mother, when was I born? You were born in winter, at dawn. Snow lay on the earth, and the sky was red. How many winters have I lived? Six winters. Soon you will guard the sheep with your uncle. Will my uncle teach me? He will teach you, and you will learn.

pie: kúdʰe toy póh₂imen ḱóymos h₁ésti? wékʷsperoy dweh₂rós h₁ésti. kʷóti nókʷtn̥s stéygʰōh₂? tísrn̥s nókʷtn̥s. kʷís gʰóstey túH? h₁eǵóh₂ poh₂imnés suHnús swóm bʰréh₂term̥ h₂isḱóh₂. kʷíd h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥? h₁sn̥tyóḱlewēs. h₁ím ǵn̥néh₃mi h₂Hséh₂i moy péruti sédt. nu moy démi ḱósyeh₂i kʷsépi légʰye h₂ewsér-kʷe gʷh₂dʰí.
english: Shepherd, where is your village? It is far away, in the west. How many nights shall I walk? Three nights. Who are you, guest? I am the son of a herdsman; I am seeking my brother. What is his name? Of-True-Fame. I know him; he sat at my hearth last year. Then lie down in my house tonight, and go at dawn.

pie: sóh₂wl̥ gʷʰermóm sḱh₃yéh₂i sédomes. dréwi Hn̥dʰí sédomes. tr̥syési? tr̥syóh₂ wódr̥ moy dh₃dʰí. ph₃dʰí. nu dinṓs dl̥h₁gʰṓs. h₁yód sóh₂wl̥ séngʷeti dṓm gʷéh₂omes. nu médʰu wékʷsperoy péh₃omes.
english: The sun is hot; let us sit in the shade. Let us sit under the tree. Are you thirsty? I am thirsty; give me water. Drink. The days are long now. When the sun goes down, we will go home. Then in the evening we will drink mead.

pie: swésor sríHgos méǵh₂ snóygʷʰos-kʷe h₂éǵroysu légʰeti. kʷóm ǵʰéyōm léyteti? h₁yód sóh₂wl̥ gʷʰéreti h₁yégos tinéh₁eti. kʷóti méh₁nsn̥s ménōmes? dwóh₁ méh₁nsh₁e. nu wósr̥ h₁ludʰḗti. wósr̥ lubʰyóh₂. h₁eǵóh₂ h₁íd éti lubʰyóh₂. kʷíd swésor wésni dʰédʰeh₁esi? h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m snéh₁oh₂ gʷéHyōh₂-kʷe.
english: Sister, the cold is great, and snow lies on the fields. When will the winter go away? When the sun grows warm, the ice will melt. How many moons shall we wait? Two moons. Then the spring will arrive. I long for the spring. I too long for it. What will you do in the spring, sister? I will spin wool, and I will sing.

pie: príHa lówksneh₂m spéḱye. h₁íh₂ drúsu upér bʰérǵʰt. h₁íh₂ ḱubʰréh₂ albʰéh₂-kʷe. túH lówksneh₂s ḱéwbʰyōs. sweh₂dúh₂ wékʷesh₂ bʰéh₂si. kʷséps góleti. gʷʰr̥néwesi me? gʷʰr̥néwoh₂ te lówksneh₂-kʷe nos spéḱyēti. kʷíd moy méh₂trey wéwkōmes? h₁ésyeh₂ey wéwkōmes lówksneh₂m spéḱyome.
english: Look at the moon, dear one! She has risen above the trees. She is beautiful and white. You are more beautiful than the moon. You speak sweet words. But the night is cold. Will you warm me? I will warm you, and the moon will watch us. What shall we tell my mother? We will tell her: we were watching the moon.
